content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Soil moisture can be estimated by fusing Sentinel-1 radar backscatter with Sentinel-2 optical imagery using change-detection algorithms to separate soil moisture signals from vegetation and surface roughness effects.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08411","field":"abstract","quote":"combines Sentinel-1 C-band backscatter with Sentinel-2 surface reflectance to estimate volumetric soil moisture content"}]},{"text":"Multi-temporal radar change-detection combined with vegetation indices from optical data achieves soil moisture retrieval with root-mean-square error of 0.034 m³/m³ and correlation of 0.79 against in-situ sensors.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08411","field":"abstract","quote":"Validation against a network of 24 in-situ TDR sensors distributed across arable fields in Serbia and Hungary showed a root-mean-square error of 0.034 m³/m³ and a correlation coefficient of 0.79"}]},{"text":"Cloud-native satellite processing architectures can deliver daily latency soil moisture products at ten-metre resolution suitable for near-real-time agricultural advisory services across continental scales.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08411","field":"abstract","quote":"Operational daily latency of the processing chain was demonstrated using cloud-based infrastructure, making the product suitable for near-real-time agricultural advisory services"}]}],"fit":"strong","fitReason":"The researcher has directly addressed the core challenge of deriving field-level soil moisture from existing satellite data by developing a Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 fusion approach that overcomes surface roughness and vegetation confounding through change-detection and vegetation correction [SYN-PUB-08411], validated against sparse in-situ networks similar to the customer's four-probe setup."}
